sourceInformation.source: Big Buck Hunter Pro (Play Mechanix / Raw Thrills arcade shooter, 2006)
sourceInformation.plan: PLAN.md (written by claude-opus-5-5 at max effort)
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade light-gun hunting shooter with party versus and bonus mini-games
sourceInformation.perspective: First person, on rails: fixed vantage per site with scripted camera pans over a pseudo-3D column landscape; side-on x-ray shot-chart cards; 2D menu and lodge screens
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript in one HTML file; my-3D2dge engine v0.85.2 (handoff package, full engine, game loop, input, audio synth, UI helpers, dialog); own pseudo-3D strip renderer; AI Hub session client 1.4.0 (lib/hub); headless Node vm tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's retro-modern outlined pixel style (480x270, shaded tones, 5x7 font); all animals, antlers, props, scopes and HUD drawn procedurally in code
sourceInformation.animation: Engine pixel drawing plus a procedural four-legged rig (two-bone leg IK, walk/trot/run gaits, graze/alert/drink poses, death fold) and engine Humanoid portraits for the cast
sourceInformation.audio: All music, sound effects and voices synthesised in code with the engine chip synth: bluegrass-flavoured chiptune songs, layered gunshots with valley echoes, animal calls, Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub session protocol v1, ghost mode: own card, 3-minute timed Hunt-Off with seeded sites, other hunters shown as ghost reticles, progress and result reporting; plays normally when no hub answers
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted tests with game.advance and game.debug (no subagents or workflows); a browser smoke check of the built file; screenshots only for what scripts cannot check
sourceInformation.research: None for this build. The plan's research (Wikipedia, Highway Games listing, Macworld review) was used as given; nothing was re-verified
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About 13 real issues across the tests and a browser smoke run: a Big Mo crash every frame, a hub-mode crash on start, flat magenta ground and trees from rgb() colour strings, a Trophy Cam that fired on every dev-spawned kill, a bot that fired 74 shots for 1 hit, a trophy the bot could never trigger, flying critters that climbed off screen, banner spam after a lost trophy, unknown input actions in dev mode, and font glyphs that printed as ?.
3 would be game breaking: the Big Mo update crash, the AI Hub round crash on start, and the magenta rendering. The rest were wrong behaviour or polish.

The scripted playthrough of the whole Hunt-Off (a cheating expert bot, confirm taps through every dialog, tally and result screen, all 15 sites and a ceremony) plus the same run in the built file with drawing on: it exercised every scene and the draw paths that headless runs skip.
The determinism hash and the 160 second attract survival check never failed and told me little; the multiplier unit checks mostly caught mistakes in my own test helpers.
engineFeedback: The fixed-step game loop with game.advance and a headless mode, so the whole game could be played and checked in Node in seconds; the chip synth with custom voices and songs; E.Dialog with live Humanoid portraits; the standard pause, settings and controls screens that cost nothing.

Yes. px colours and E.tones want #rrggbb: an rgb() string made E.tones and E.hex return NaN and the ground drew magenta with no error. Input actions must be declared up front, and the pad glyph and device helpers took some reading. The overlay draw is not run headless, so draw bugs only showed in the browser.

The first-person view: a column terrain renderer with depth strips, billboards, fog, scope lens passes and occlusion-correct shot picking, plus the four-legged animal rig with gaits, hit zones and antlers, the animal AI and the bot.

Fitting a pseudo-3D first-person shooter into a 2D engine built for ground, side and iso views: the engine has no camera model for it, so the world, hit testing and depth sorting are all the game's own.
Nothing. The engine file is the handoff copy unmodified; everything new lives in the game sources.

A first-person pseudo-3D view type (heightfield, billboards, fog, mouse picking) with the Mode 7 style view cache, so shooters like this need less custom rendering. Accepting CSS colour strings in px and E.tones would also have saved me an hour.
promptFeedback: The clear deliverable list (one file, exit interview JSON, named sections), the freedom to cut the plan, and the strong steer to test headless with game.advance and game.debug.

The plan names a different output file and dev folder (opus, 2026-11-03) than TASK.md and STAGE.md ask for; I followed TASK.md. The plan is far larger than a medium-effort session can build, and it does not say which parts are essential.

Scope: 27 systems, three hunts, trophies, bonus games, a range, dev mode, attract mode, local four-player and an AI Hub round with the one 10-foot controller-first UI, all in one session without an art pipeline.

Mark the essential systems of a plan against optional ones, state how much work a build stage should expect, and name one output file in all the documents. Say how to count usage so the Usage line is not always unknown.

aiHub.name: BIG BUCK HUNT-OFF
aiHub.description: A first-person arcade hunting shooter: spot the bucks, shoot clean, pump, never shoot a doe. Three hunts with trophies and bonus games, an x-ray shot chart, one-screen party play and a timed AI Hub Hunt-Off.
aiHub.controls: Aim: mouse, WASD or left stick · Fire: click, Space or R2 · Pump: R or Square · Scope: right click or L2 · Call: E or Triangle
